extracted.intended_audience: AAAI-26 authors, reviewers, senior program committee (SPC) members, and area chairs (ACs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural standards for using an AI-powered multi-step workflow to generate factual, non-scored reviews of conference paper submissions, and how those AI outputs interact with human reviewers and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to AAAI review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review system analyses the paper "in accordance with the AAAI review criteria" before generating the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated reviews are intended to follow the same guidelines given to human reviewers and be factual; however, the AI will NOT provide any scores, ratings, or recommendations and subjective judgments remain with human reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper pre-processing and structured parsing
rubrics_metrics.description: All paper PDFs are resampled to a fixed resolution and converted into a structured markdown using an ML-based OCR trained on scientific PDFs; both the tokenized raw file and the markdown are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The markdown extracts math notation and equations into LaTeX and preserves table layouts to enable accurate downstream technical parsing and multimodal interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary story analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary analysis of the story of the paper: the problem being addressed, the stated limitations of the state of the art, the key innovations in the paper, and the proofs or empirical evaluations that support the conclusions of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stage focuses on summarizing problem, contributions, and supporting evidence to frame subsequent technical checks and literature comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks for factual, mathematical, and algorithmic correctness, including the equations, pseudocode, and figures in the technical presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A code interpreter is available to the LLM to assist in verifying computations, equations, and algorithmic claims; this is aimed at identifying factual or logical errors in the technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search and related-work assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Performing several rounds of literature search of published papers using keyword search to examine the contributions of the paper relative to prior work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search results are used to evaluate novelty, contextualize claims, and identify missing related work or incorrect citations; the literature tool is primarily for retrieval, not explicit reference verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results checking (figures/tables/text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Checks the results section, including all figures, tables, and text descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifies that reported results are consistent across text, tables, and figures and looks for obvious inconsistencies or misrepresentations in how results are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-critique of generated review
rubrics_metrics.description: A stage that reviews the review itself to check for factual accuracy, consistency with the paper, and any unsubstantiated claims; revisions are made to address issues found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AI performs internal consistency checks and edits to reduce hallucinations and unsupported assertions before the review is released to humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal interpretation capability
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI system uses multimodal LLMs and multiple input formats (raw tokenized PDF and structured markdown) to interpret images, graphical content, tables, math, and code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining modalities and structured markdown improves the system's ability to parse specialized notation, figures, and tables; nevertheless, subjective judgments on novelty or impact are left to humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: No scoring or recommendations provided by AI
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review will NOT provide any scores, ratings, or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AI is intended to be a factual aid following human review guidelines; final decisions and subjective recommendations are made by human PC members, SPCs, and ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy and data handling safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI-26 will only utilize AI systems via APIs whose provider guarantees that queries (including submissions and prompts) remain private and will neither be used to train future models nor used for any other purpose except producing outputs for the AI review; manuscripts are stored only on OpenReview and ephemeral copies are retrieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendor contracts are required to guarantee no storage or logging beyond generation of the AI review; authors must still submit anonymous PDFs per author instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human accountability and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Humans retain final decision-making authority; SPC members are responsible for excluding content considered harmful, and humans are solely responsible for decisions in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI outputs are inspected by SPCs and human reviewers; the rebuttal and discussion phases are used to resolve differences and ensure human consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias and ethical-violation inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated reviews, like human reviews, will be inspected by SPCs to flag ethical violations or inappropriate content, including statements indicating bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee will actively inspect AI outputs for amplification of linguistic, geographic, or topical biases baked into LLM training data, and flag issues for human handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitations: plagiarism and reference verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review system is not intended to check for plagiarism; although it uses a literature search tool, the tool is primarily to retrieve related work rather than to explicitly check references. Ethical issues may be flagged but are not the primary intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate automated and semi-automated checks in the overall AAAI review process are responsible for explicit plagiarism detection and other policy enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of complex, specialized content
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI parses raw and structured markdown to verify complex proofs, specialized notation, and domain terminology, but does not make subjective judgments—those remain with human reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI assists in parsing and surface-level verification of technical content but is limited in context retention and domain coverage; humans use their expertise to render subjective assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial-attack detection and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI system has explicit safeguards (both AI- and classical approach based) to detect and flag hidden prompts, data poisoning, or other adversarial attacks within manuscripts and has been tested against known adversarial attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are detection mechanisms in the workflow to identify potential adversarial inputs; flagged issues are subject to human review and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesis across multiple models/tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review is generated over multiple steps using different models, tools, and prompts at each stage, but is synthesized into a single final review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple-model outputs are combined into one coherent review; differences between model outputs are expected to be resolved in human discussion phases if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of AI authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review will be clearly marked to indicate which portions were generated by AI systems versus humans, and who is ultimately accountable for the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling improves transparency for authors and reviewers; accountability for decisions remains with humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author rebuttal and appeal mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit a rebuttal to the AI review just like they do for a human review; the AI review will not be updated based on the authors' response, but human reviewers can read the response and take it into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major issues that warrant oversight from conference staff can be flagged using the 'comment' field visible to SPCs and above.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pre-submission author access and no acceptance estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors cannot submit their papers to the AI system before submission to estimate acceptance chances, and the AI system will neither estimate chances of acceptance nor provide any recommendations or scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AI tool is restricted to the conference review pipeline and is not a public or pre-submission recommendation tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational consistency and update policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The AI review generation algorithm will not be updated mid-cycle; the deployment system is designed to be interruptible and resumable to handle network or server issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy aims to ensure consistency across reviewed papers during a conference cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback, evaluation, and post-event reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: AAAI will solicit feedback from authors, reviewers, SPCs, and ACs and produce a technical report summarizing design, deployment, feedback, impact, and qualitative findings after the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report will include findings based on review questionnaires and community feedback to iterate on the AI-assisted review program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging and reporting of financial and environmental costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial costs of the AI systems will be cumulatively logged and reported; the environmental impact will be estimated using accepted methods based on model usage and compute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs and impact assessments will be documented in technical reports to maintain accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and validation of the workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The workflow has been tested using public papers and reviews, specially crafted test-case papers to surface specific errors (e.g., mathematical/logical errors), multiple sampling for consistency, and testing for robustness to adversarial inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive pre-deployment testing is part of the validation regime to improve reliability and detect weaknesses before live use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output specificity and evidence-based statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors will receive the review generated by the AI review system, and the review will include specifics to justify or substantiate any points raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI reviews should state evidence and cite parts of the paper (e.g., figures, equations) to substantiate claims, enabling human reviewers and authors to verify assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human ability to rate/comment on AI reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, reviewers, SPCs, and ACs will have the opportunity to rate and comment on the AI reviews if they wish, to provide feedback on the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community feedback mechanisms are provided to collect qualitative assessments of AI review usefulness and quality.
